roles.name: Supporter
roles.note: Assigned to signed-up app users (id referenced directly by DIRECTUS_SUPPORTER_ROLE_ID in the website's env for signup — that env var is the source of truth for which role this is, since Directus role names can be changed in the admin UI and this one already has been once, from 'Refuge App User'). Owns the 'Supporter - Own Favourites' and 'Supporter - Chat Read' policies.

roles.name: Chat Service
roles.note: Dedicated service role for the Next.js moderation server. Only this role can write to the chat collection directly. Create one Directus user with this role and generate a static token for it — that token goes in the Next.js app's server env, never in the mobile app.

directusUsers.note: Supporter/membership fields added directly to the built-in directus_users collection (1:1 with a user, no need for a separate join collection). Written only by the Next.js membership webhook using an admin-level token — see scripts/stripe/provision-supporter-prices.mjs in refuge-worldwide for the Stripe side.

meta.note: Set by the membership webhook only.
Mirrors the Stripe subscription status enum.

Set by the membership webhook when Stripe reports a failed invoice payment (Stripe itself emails the user — this is just so we can flag it on their account). Cleared once a subsequent sync reports the subscription active again.

policies.name: Supporter - Own Membership Read
policies.note: Lets a signed-in user read their own supporter/subscription status (needed for the account page), but never write it — only the membership webhook can do that.

policies.name: Supporter - Own Profile Update
policies.note: Lets a signed-in user update their own display name (stored in first_name) and password. Added after discovering the read-only policy above didn't cover the website's settings page.

meta.note: Per-user favourited shows. One row per (user, show_id) pair.
Immutable show ID from the content API (not the slug).

policies.name: Supporter - Own Favourites
policies.note: Lets an authenticated user create/read/delete only their own favourite rows.

meta.note: Site-wide settings. Currently just the supporter discount codes shown on the app's account screen.
Repeater of discount codes shown to paid supporters in the app (Copy Discount Code button). Each row: { label, code }.

policies.name: Supporter - Settings Read
policies.note: Lets any signed-in app user read the settings singleton via the API (currently just discount_codes). Deliberately NOT attached to Public — this is what keeps the discount codes out of the public API. Directus permissions can't filter this unrelated singleton by the requester's subscription_status, so the app itself further restricts the Copy Discount Code button to paid supporters (see AuthContext isPaidSupporter) on top of this signed-in-only API gate. 'id' must stay in the fields list even though the app never requests it: Directus 500s ('An unexpected error occurred') reading a singleton when the field permission list excludes the primary key — confirmed by testing as an actual Supporter-role user.

meta.note: Live chat messages. Written only by the moderation server, never directly by clients.
Optional image URL attached to the message.

The actual human sender, resolved server-side from the caller's Directus token via readMe() and set explicitly by the moderation server. Never accept this as a client-supplied value. Not the Directus 'user_created' field, which would just show the service account for every row.

policies.name: Supporter - Chat Read
policies.note: Public and signed-in users can read the chat feed. Nobody can write directly — that only happens through the moderation server.

policies.name: Refuge App - Chat Server Write
policies.note: Only the moderation server's dedicated Directus user (role: Chat Service) can create chat messages, after resolving the real sender server-side and running its own moderation checks. The 'user' and (for signed-in senders) 'username' fields must be set from the server's own token verification, never trusted from the client request body. Also needs read: the server's own rate-limit check (lib/chatModeration.ts) queries recent messages by this same token before allowing a create.
